tasks.spec:
You are adding a MASTER TIMELINE stage to the OBE podcast pipeline at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. Do NOT git commit, git push, or open a PR. Do NOT send anything externally or publish. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Subscription/OAuth only, zero API spend. Set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp for everything you run.

FILES YOU OWN: server/pipeline/av_sync.py and tests/test_av_sync.py. You may ALSO write these outputs and nothing else outside your task directory: /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/timeline.json and /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/stems/*. DO NOT modify composite_side_by_side or anything else in video_assembly.py; wiring the composite onto the stems is a separate later task and is explicitly out of scope for you.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Five composites of this episode shipped with broken audio. The owner heard the guest speaking three minutes and forty-five seconds before he joined the room, the two speakers talking over each other, and dead air. The root cause is architectural, not a bad filter string: the pipeline goes from four raw WebM tracks to one 730MB mixed master in a single ffmpeg invocation, so there is no intermediate artifact anyone can check, and the video half of that invocation gets TWO steps while the audio half gets ONE. Video is normalized first (setpts reset + fps=30, which fills dropouts by holding frames) and only then placed at its offset with tpad. Audio has to do both jobs in one filter expression, and no single ffmpeg audio filter can. asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS keeps the join offset and DELETES the dropouts. aresample=async=1:first_pts=0 fills the dropouts and DELETES the join offset. Both together shift the late joiner twice. All three were measured on this episode and all three are wrong.

YOUR JOB IS TO GIVE AUDIO THE SAME TWO STEPS VIDEO ALREADY HAS, and to write the timeline down as a checkable artifact first.

MEASURED GROUND TRUTH for episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/raw (four *.webm sorted by name; index 0 host audio, 1 host video, 2 guest audio, 3 guest video). Derive all of this in code; it is given here so you can tell immediately if your derivation is wrong:
  host_audio   first packet    0.225s  last packet 2842.396s  ONE dropout at 151.86s lasting 76.86s
  host_video   first packet    0.229s  last packet 2842.421s  dropouts: 20.73s+4.19s, 25.68s+203.92s, then eleven of about 1.1s
  guest_audio  first packet  224.875s  last packet 2841.240s  no dropouts
  guest_video  first packet  224.896s  last packet 2841.228s  no dropouts
  grid T=0 = 0.225s (earliest first packet). SESSION LENGTH = 2842.196s.
The host's camera is genuinely dead for 203.9 seconds and his mic for 76.9 seconds; both recover within five seconds of the guest joining. That is real source content and must be PRESERVED as held frames and silence, never skipped. IMPORTANT: ffprobe reports container duration as 0.000 for all four files because Daily writes live streams with no duration header. Track extent must come from the first and last PACKET timestamps, never from the duration field.

STAGE 1 - derive_timeline. Add a function to server/pipeline/av_sync.py that probes a raw directory and returns the master timeline, plus a writer that saves it to processed/timeline.json. Derive every number from ffprobe packet timestamps. A dropout is any gap larger than 0.4s between the end of one packet and the start of the next. Cross-check each track's container start_time against the epoch milliseconds in its filename minus the session id that prefixes it (for example 1784728761801 minus 1784728761538 = 0.263s); if those two witnesses disagree by more than 0.100s, RAISE and refuse to build stems, because then the join time is not trustworthy. EXACT schema, because an executed check parses it:
{"version": 1, "episode": "2026-06-10-fred-cho", "session": {"t0_abs_s": float, "end_abs_s": float, "length_s": float}, "tracks": {"<role>": {"file": "basename.webm", "kind": "audio"|"video", "participant": "host"|"guest", "container_start_s": float, "filename_epoch_offset_s": float, "first_pts_s": float, "last_pts_s": float, "grid_offset_s": float, "content_s": float, "hole_total_s": float, "holes": [{"at_abs_s": float, "duration_s": float}]}}, "stems": {"<role>": "stems/<role>.<ext>"}}
The four roles are exactly host_audio, host_video, guest_audio, guest_video. grid_offset_s is that track's first packet minus session t0_abs_s. Extra fields are fine; missing ones are not.

STAGE 2 - four grid-aligned stems, TWO STEPS EACH, into processed/stems/. Name them host_audio, host_video, guest_audio, guest_video with whatever extension you choose (FLAC for audio and mp4 for video are sensible; audio 48kHz stereo, video 960x540 at 30fps to match _normalize_composite_camera's geometry). Every stem must be EXACTLY session length (2842.196s) and start at grid T=0, so all four are interchangeable timelines and a cut is the same timestamp on all four.
  AUDIO step A - produce a gapless track that starts at zero with its dropouts materialized as silence. aresample=async=1:first_pts=0 does exactly this and is correct HERE, in isolation, where there is no offset for it to destroy. ASSERT the result before continuing: its length must equal that track's packet span (last_pts minus first_pts) within 0.2s. For host_audio that is 2842.171s, which is 76.86s longer than the 2763.54s a plain decode produces. If you get 2763s, the dropout was deleted and you must stop and fix step A.
  AUDIO step B - place it and pad the tail: shift by grid_offset_s and extend to session length. adelay plus apad, then a hard -t at session length. ASSERT the result is session length.
  VIDEO step A - reuse the existing recipe in video_assembly._normalize_composite_camera (setpts=PTS-STARTPTS, fps=30, scale, pad); fps=30 is timestamp-aware and holds frames across dropouts, which is why video already works. Do not import it if that creates a cycle; reimplement the same filter chain in av_sync. ASSERT the result equals the track's packet span.
  VIDEO step B - shift by grid_offset_s with black, extend the tail to session length, hard -t. ASSERT session length.
Asserting after EACH step is the point. That is what nobody did for five builds.

STAGE 3 - tests. Extend tests/test_av_sync.py with unit tests that need no media: the timeline derivation must reject a track whose filename epoch and container start disagree by more than 100ms; grid offsets must be computed relative to the earliest track; and the audio stem recipe must be two distinct steps, never a single filter that combines first_pts=0 with adelay. Keep the existing regression tests unless your design genuinely invalidates one, and if so replace its guarantee and say why in the docstring. Never delete a regression test without replacing it.

THE RECEIPT you must satisfy, and should run yourself as you go:
  python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/podcast-full-auto/stems_check.py
It re-derives every timeline number from the raw packets independently, so a hand-written or fabricated timeline.json fails. It then asserts all four stems are session length; that the guest's audio stem is under 2% of his speaking energy at 30s, 120s and 184s (he does not join until 224.65s); that the guest's video stem is black there; that the host's audio stem is under 2% of speaking energy inside his 76.9s dropout while being loud on both sides of it; that the host's audio still lands where the timeline says at raw second 2000; and that the host's video frames 164 seconds apart inside his camera dropout are near-identical, proving the dropout was held rather than skipped. The silence assertion has already been validated against a deliberately-broken stem: a guest stem built by plain decode reads 12-41% of speaking energy at those probes and is caught, while a correctly delayed one reads exactly 0.00.

Budget your iterations. A full four-stem build takes roughly 10-20 minutes, dominated by the two video re-encodes. Prototype and assert the AUDIO stems first, which take about a minute each, and only then spend time on video.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH and paste the real terminal output into your final message: the receipt command above, and `cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp python3 -m pytest tests/test_av_sync.py -q -p no:cacheprovider`. A claim without executed output is not done. Leave the working tree dirty; the coordinator reviews and lands it.
tasks.verified: timeline.json is re-derived from the raw packet timestamps by an independent check, and all four stems span the full 2842.196s session on one grid with the late joiner silent and black before he joins and both host dropouts filled rather than deleted
